title: Enriched conical colimits of marked objects under universe enlargement
statement:
Fix nested Grothendieck universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ as in [def-weil-size-convention], a $\mathcal U$-small marked simplicial set $(B,S)$, and the marked simplicial sets and sharp marking of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. For $\mathcal W=\mathcal U,\mathcal U'$, let $\mathsf M_{\mathcal W}$ be the category of $\mathcal W$-small marked simplicial sets over $(B,S)$, with marking-preserving maps over the base. Its simplicial enrichment has
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_B(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{/(B,S)}(X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Y),$$
and tensor $T\otimes X=T^\sharp\times X$, with base map ignoring $T$. Let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial category (objects, mapping simplicial sets and associative unital composition), and let $F:I\to\mathsf M_{\mathcal U}$ be a simplicial enriched functor. An enriched conical colimit is an object $L$ with an enriched cocone such that, naturally in $Y$, $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_B(L,Y)$ is the simplicial set of enriched transformations $F\to\Delta_IY$; its $n$-simplices are families $F_i\otimes\Delta^n\to Y$ compatible with the $I$-actions. This is the enriched adjunction convention of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams].

The enriched conical colimit of $F$ exists in $\mathsf M_{\mathcal U}$. Viewing it and its cocone in $\mathcal U'$ gives an enriched conical colimit of the included diagram in $\mathsf M_{\mathcal U'}$. The comparison is natural in $F$, and is a comparison of the cocones and their enriched adjunctions, valid against arbitrary $\mathcal U'$-small targets $Y$. The assertion includes the empty simplicial category $I$.

source.place: Enriched tensor and conical-colimit adjunction conventions of Appendix A.3.1 and A.3.3; ordinary enriched coproduct/coequalizer construction. The marked-over-base universe comparison is agent-written, not asserted as a separately numbered result in HTT. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text:
Write $F_i=(X_i,M_i)\to(B,S)$. The tensor convention gives an action map $a_{ij}:I(i,j)^\sharp\times F_i\to F_j$ over $(B,S)$. Explicitly, for $u\in I(i,j)_r$, let $a_{ij}(u,x)$ be the value at $(x,\mathrm{id}_{[r]})$ of the marked map $F_i\times(\Delta^r)^\sharp\to F_j$ represented by the image of $u$ under the enriched functor. This commutes with all simplicial operators. For $r=1$ and $x\in M_i$ its value is marked, since that representing map preserves markings. Form the underlying simplicial objects over $B$
$$C=\coprod_iX_i,\qquad A=\coprod_{i,j}I(i,j)\times X_i.$$
These are small coproducts in the simplicial slice, which exist and are degreewise coproducts by [lem-coef-sset-pullback-preserves-colimits]. Give $C$ the union of the images of $M_i$ and give each summand of $A$ the product marking: $(u,x)$ is marked precisely when $x\in M_i$. Projection to $X_i$ followed by its coproduct inclusion defines $d_0:A\to C$; the actions followed by inclusion of $X_j$ define $d_1:A\to C$. Both maps are over $(B,S)$ and preserve markings.

source.place: Definitions 3.1.0.1 and A.3.1.5; agent-written action and coproduct construction, step 1.

proof.text:
Take the coequalizer $q:C\to L$ of the underlying pair $d_0,d_1$ in simplicial sets over $B$, using [lem-coef-sset-pullback-preserves-colimits]. Its degreewise set construction can be chosen as
$$L_r=C_r/{\sim_r},\qquad (i,x)\sim_r(j,a_{ij}(u,x))\quad(u\in I(i,j)_r),$$
where $\sim_r$ is the equivalence relation generated by the displayed pairs. The simplicial operators act on classes by those of $C$: they take every generating pair to the corresponding pair for the image of $u$, and hence respect finite zigzags of generating pairs and their reverses. The simplicial identities hold on representatives. The base map is $[i,x]\mapsto p_i(x)$, well-defined since the actions are over $B$. Mark exactly the edges in $q_1(\coprod_iM_i)$. Every degenerate edge is marked: its vertex lifts to some $(i,x_0)$, and its degeneracy is $q_1(i,s_0x_0)$. The base map preserves this marking because each $p_i$ does.

source.place: Definition 3.1.0.1 and Appendix A.3.3 conventions; agent-written marked coequalizer construction, step 2.

proof.text:
Let $\lambda_i:F_i\to L$ be inclusion followed by $q$. They preserve markings by their definition. For every $i,j,r,u,x$ the relation gives
$$\lambda_j(a_{ij}(u,x))=\lambda_i(x).$$
This is equality of simplicial maps $I(i,j)^\sharp\times F_i\to L$, so the $\lambda_i$ are an enriched cocone. In particular the equation uses every simplex of $I(i,j)$, rather than just the vertices of its underlying ordinary category.

source.place: Appendix A.3.3 enriched-functor convention; agent verification of the cocone equations, step 3.

proof.text:
Fix either universe, any marked object $Y\to(B,S)$ in that universe, and $n\geq0$. By the enriched-transformation convention, an $n$-simplex of the cocone mapping object is a family of marked maps $h_i:F_i\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Y$ over the base such that, in every degree $r$,
$$h_j(a_{ij}(u,x),t)=h_i(x,t)\quad(u\in I(i,j)_r,\ x\in(X_i)_r,\ t\in(\Delta^n)_r).$$
Define $h_r:L_r\times(\Delta^n)_r\to Y_r$ by $h_r([i,x],t)=h_i(x,t)$. This is well-defined: the displayed equation gives equal values across one generating pair at a fixed $t$, and thus along any finite zigzag. For every simplicial operator $\theta$, one has $\theta h_i(x,t)=h_i(\theta x,\theta t)$; this proves on representatives that $h$ is simplicial. Its base map is the prescribed map $L\to B$. Uniqueness holds because every class has a representative.

source.place: Appendix A.3.3 enriched natural transformations; direct quotient descent with the parameter held fixed, step 4.

proof.text: The descended map $h:L\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Y$ preserves markings. Indeed, a marked edge of its source is $(\ell,t)$ with $\ell=q_1(i,x)$ for a marked edge $x\in M_i$ and with arbitrary $t\in(\Delta^n)_1$. Its image is $h_i(x,t)$, which is marked because $h_i$ is a marked map. Conversely, restriction of any marked $h$ along $\lambda_i\times\mathrm{id}$ is marked and satisfies the equation of step 4 by step 3. The restriction and descent operations are inverse, as is seen by evaluating at every $([i,x],t)$.

source.place: Definition 3.1.0.1 and the sharp/product marking; direct marking check, step 5.

proof.text: These inverse bijections in degree $n$ form an isomorphism of simplicial sets. For an operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, both routes send a family $h_i$ to the map $([i,x],t)\mapsto h_i(x,\alpha(t))$; hence they commute with faces and degeneracies. Postcomposition with $v:Y\to Z$ commutes with descent, since both values are $v(h_i(x,t))$. More generally a simplicial parameter $v:Y\times(\Delta^k)^\sharp\to Z$ gives on simultaneous parameters the identical formula $v(h_i(x,t),s)$, so this is enriched naturality in $Y$. The isomorphism is restriction along the actual cocone $\lambda$, and therefore identifies its enriched adjunction, in the convention of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams]. This proves that the constructed cocone is an enriched conical colimit.

source.place: Appendix A.3.1 and A.3.3 adjunction conventions; verification on parameters of the representing isomorphism, step 6.

proof.text: All the input sets in $A_r,C_r$ belong to $\mathcal U$: the objects of $I$, its mapping simplicial sets, and the $X_i$ are $\mathcal U$-small. Grothendieck-universe closure under small indexed unions, products, and subsets puts the equivalence relations, their sets of equivalence classes, the countable simplicial data, and the marking of $L$ in $\mathcal U$. Use this very same quotient and marking in $\mathcal U'$. The relation remains the same: a finite zigzag of elements of the fixed $C_r$ uses only elements of $\mathcal U$, even if considered in $\mathcal U'$. Steps 4-6 apply to arbitrary $\mathcal U'$-small $Y$, since their formulas and finite-zigzag check place no bound on the size of $Y$. Thus the included cocone, with the same restriction isomorphisms, is colimiting in the larger universe as well. This verifies the adjunction against larger targets directly.

source.place: Agent-written universe bookkeeping for the quotient construction; universes as in the item and def-weil-size-convention, step 7.

proof.text: For an enriched natural transformation $\eta:F\to G$, define $L(\eta)[i,x]=[i,\eta_i(x)]$. Naturality gives $\eta_j(a^F_{ij}(u,x))=a^G_{ij}(u,\eta_i(x))$, so a generating relation maps to a generating relation. The map is simplicial and over the base on representatives, and sends the class of a marked edge to that of a marked edge. Identity and composition laws follow from the same formula. A transformation with a simplicial parameter has the formula $([i,x],t)\mapsto[i,\eta_i(x,t)]$, with the identical checks. These formulas are identical in the two universes; restriction of mapping objects to the cocones therefore commutes with the comparison in $F$ as well as in $Y$. If other colimit apices are chosen, the degree-zero universal property gives the unique isomorphism carrying these cocones to those apices; its two composites are identities because they agree on all $\lambda_i$. Restriction along it identifies the same enriched adjunctions in every degree. Uniqueness on the cocone legs also makes these comparison isomorphisms natural in $F$.

source.place: Agent-written naturality of the quotient and uniqueness of the comparison, step 8.

proof.text: When $I$ has no objects, $A=C=L=\varnothing$ in every degree and the marking of $L$ is empty. Its product with every $(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ is empty, so there is exactly one marked map over $(B,S)$ from it to any $Y$. An empty family of components is likewise unique in every degree, and all simplicial operators preserve this unique element. Both mapping objects are therefore the terminal simplicial set, in either universe, and the unique empty cocone has the required enriched universal property.

source.place: Direct empty-diagram check for the same construction, step 9.

proof_origin.place: Definitions 3.1.0.1, A.3.1.5 and Appendix A.3.3 supply the conventions only; steps 1-9 are the explicit marked-over-base quotient proof, including arbitrary larger targets. No separately numbered source theorem asserts this universe comparison.

Step 5 picks a marked representative of each marked edge, which is required because other representatives need not be marked. Step 6 gives an isomorphism of simplicial sets that is enriched-natural in Y, not only a bijection on vertices. Step 7: the generated relation does not depend on the universe because zigzags are finite, and nothing bounds the size of Y. Steps 8 and 9 (naturality in F, empty I) are correct.
